key_insight: An applied electric field can tune magnon-mediated spin photocurrent in Cr2O3 by modifying the Dzyaloshinsky–Moriya interaction and thus the spin-current conductivity.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a route to electrically controllable spin photovoltaic devices, where polarization-dependent photocurrent can be actively tuned in magnetoelectric oxides.
method: Used nonlinear response theory to model magnon spin photocurrent in Cr2O3.
Analyzed how an external electric field induces Dzyaloshinsky–Moriya interaction and spin canting.
Compared resonance frequency, peak intensity, and polarization anisotropy under varying electric field.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports field-dependent shifts in resonance frequency and peak intensity, plus a two-magnon continuum spectrum from field-induced spin canting.
watch_item: The results are theoretical for a specific magnetoelectric oxide, so experimental validation and material/device integration may be challenging.
paper_title: Electrical control of spin photocurrent in a magnetoelectric oxide Cr$_2$O$_3$
